Symphony No. 5 in C minor. Perhaps the most famous work in the entire classical music repertoire, Ludwig van Beethoven's Symphony No. 5, Op. 67, completed in 1808, is universally recognized by its dramatic opening motif—three short notes followed by one long note. This motif repeats and builds throughout the entire first movement.

The symphony traces a psychological journey from the dark, turbulent key of C minor to a triumphant, brass-heavy C major in the finale. The opening motif follows a short-short-short-long pattern, with the first statement played fortissimo in unison by the strings and clarinets as G-G-G-E-flat. A famous description attributes to Beethoven the phrase "Fate Knocking at the Door" to describe this opening motif, though modern musicologists widely doubt this anecdote. Beethoven supposedly told his secretary Anton Schindler about it, but the story's authenticity is questionable.

The first movement is written in sonata-allegro form, with the entire movement generated from the opening four-note cells. It features a sudden, expressive solo oboe cadenza in the recapitulation. The third movement is a scherzo in C minor featuring a dramatic horn call and a trio with fugal cellos. The movement ends with a soft, mysterious bridge led by a tapping timpani. An attacca transition connects this third movement directly to the fourth without pause, resolving the tension into C major.

The fourth movement is a triumphant march that expanded the Classical orchestra by introducing the piccolo, contrabassoon, and trombones into a symphony for the first time. The work premiered at a marathon concert in Vienna in December 1808, establishing Beethoven as a revolutionary figure who expanded the emotional and structural limits of the symphonic form.

During World War II, the BBC popularized the opening motif as a symbol of Allied resistance and victory. The rhythm of three short beats and one long beat matches the Morse code for the letter V, representing victory. In 1977, the first movement was recorded and included on the Voyager Golden Record, sent into deep space to represent human achievement. The work forms a central piece in Beethoven's middle heroic period.
